extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers, especially short story authors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing satisfying conclusions to short stories that resonate with readers; covers thematic closure, conflict resolution vs. ambiguity, emotional payoff, twists, simplicity, and circular structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect the Theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Tie the ending back to the central theme of your story so the conclusion reflects and enhances what the story is really about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the conclusion doesn't feel disconnected from the heart of your story; amplify and bring the theme full circle. Examples: if the story is about personal growth, show self-realization; if about loss, evoke bittersweet emotions. Use the ending to offer deeper understanding of the core idea or message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve the Conflict (Or Not)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the central conflict in a way that feels earned and believable; resolution can be neat, subtle, unexpected, or deliberately unresolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers expect some closure on the main conflict, but full resolution isn't always required—ambiguous endings can add depth and invite contemplation. Balance is crucial: leave space for readers to reflect, but avoid leaving so many loose threads that readers feel frustrated. The resolution should feel plausible given the story and character arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create Emotional Resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft an ending that leaves readers feeling something—joy, sadness, shock, reflection—by focusing on the characters' emotional journey and how they've changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the emotional payoff to the journey the reader has taken; deliver catharsis when the story builds toward it, or choose a quiet, understated ending for subtle impact. Emotional depth doesn't require melodrama; a restrained ending can be powerful if it reflects honest internal growth or loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subvert Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a twist or reversal to catch readers off guard, but only if the surprise feels earned and emerges organically from the story and characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant clues 'hidden in plain sight' so the reveal makes sense on reread. Avoid twists purely for shock value—they can feel gimmicky or forced and undermine the narrative. A good twist should deepen the story and give readers an 'aha' moment that encourages re-reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace Simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes a simple, understated conclusion is more effective than a grand or intricate ending—especially in short stories where economy of language matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don't need to tie up every subplot or explain every detail; a single well-chosen image, line of dialogue, or character action can leave a lasting impact. Apply the spirit of Hemingway's 'Iceberg Theory'—leave meaning beneath the surface and let readers draw conclusions rather than spelling everything out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circular Structure: Bring It Full Circle
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a sense of symmetry and completeness by echoing the story's beginning in the ending—revisit imagery, tone, or situations to show the protagonist's journey coming full circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repetition or mirrored elements (an image, a line, a situation) from the opening to reinforce cohesion and thematic unity. Example: a character who began by making a mistake ends having learned from it, signaling growth and closure through circularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the Ending Feel True to the Story (Authenticity and Lasting Impression)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ending should feel authentic—true to the story you've told—and leave a lasting impression that lingers after the last word is read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose resolution, emotional depth, a twist, or simplicity based on what fits the story rather than what feels clever. Understand your characters and theme, and strike the right balance between closure and mystery. Practice and thoughtful revision will help create endings that resonate and make readers want to reflect or re-read.
